findings.reason: The protected source stores encoded strings and constructs every split candidate eagerly. Python string concatenation copies O(n) characters across O(n^3) split transitions, and the O(n^2) table can retain O(n^3) characters. Its actual worst-case O(n^4) time and O(n^3) character storage therefore do not meet the manifest's O(n^3)-time and O(n^2)-space contract.

The inert candidate preserves the complete interval recurrence and strict-improvement tie order while storing only minimum lengths and compact literal, split, or repeat decisions. It reconstructs once through a pieces list and join, which makes the documented O(n^3) time and O(n^2) auxiliary space true without changing the app-local solve(s) contract.

Metadata consistently identifies Premium LeetCode problem 471, its Python string method, and its single nonempty lowercase-string input. The candidate returns one shortest representation that decodes to the input, leaves non-beneficial repetitions literal, and correctly permits any tied minimum answer under the source contract.

The protected app source and immutable native source bound to verified submission 2064971612 are algorithmically identical: both process interval widths, test every split, find the shortest period with doubled-text search, use the optimal period-prefix state, and replace only on strict improvement. The candidate retains that recurrence and ordering but changes the table payload and reconstruction data flow; it remains inert and cannot replace either protected artifact without separate authorization and remote Accepted evidence for exact staged native bytes.

The length-6, length-12, and length-24 near-uniform workloads span 4x and isolate repeated interval and period work. The exact candidate passed all 9 correctness cases and all three performance tiers, including the newly authored legal length-150 boundary. A correct manual-character period O(n^4) control passed every output but failed only the runtime verdict with relative growth exponent +0.23.

The candidate-targeted Approach exactly follows encoded_length, decision, the ascending-width interval order, literal baseline, split and shortest-period costs, strict tie behavior, recursive emission, and final join. Its induction covers all outermost encoding forms, and its O(n^3)-time and O(n^2)-space analysis accounts for period search and one-time reconstruction.

The hash-bound modular Reference was checked directly through the authenticated Premium statement. It preserves the positive-integer repetition syntax, exact-repeat and nested-encoding semantics, strictly-shorter rule, tied-answer allowance, all three examples and explanations in order, both constraints, and the absence of visuals, tables, or later source sections.

coverage: All three authenticated Premium source examples now appear first and in source order with exact input and output facts, including the previously missing 10[a] output. Each is explicitly tagged as a source example.

The shortest-string validator preserves the source's tied-output contract by requiring valid nested repetition syntax, exact decoding, strict shortening for every encoded region, and the same minimum length as the authored expected output.

Boundaries cover string lengths 1 and 150 and the lowercase alphabet endpoints a and z. Visible cases also cover non-beneficial repetition, one- and multi-character units, two- and three-digit counts, a compressed prefix with literal suffix, nested encoding, and a string with no repetition.

An independent divisor-enumerating minimum-length oracle verified all nine authored results and all three benchmark outputs. It also agreed with current and candidate sources on 1,022 exhaustive binary strings and 1,000 deterministic randomized lowercase strings.
All nine correctness cases are visible samples or trials; the unchanged length-6, length-12, and length-24 near-uniform workloads remain hidden and performance-only in benchmark.json.
